advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Catch `CriteriaError` (or its aliases) alongside `LLMError` around the registry lookups in `_criteria_eval` so a malformed criteria overlay yields a clean error + exit 1.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:165-167: only `except LLMError as exc:` wraps this block
src/rebar/llm/criteria/model.py:37: `class CriteriaError(Exception):` — NOT a subclass of `LLMError`
src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:288-322: `effective_criteria` raises `CriteriaError` for a non-list `activate`, a non-string activation id, or an activated id with no routing entry
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:337-338: `by_id` calls `load_criteria(repo_root)` which resolves every criterion's prompt
advisory.finding: `CriteriaError` raised by `code_review_registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)` (and `plan_review_registry.by_id`) is not caught by the `except LLMError` handler, so a malformed `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` now crashes `rebar criteria eval` with an unhandled traceback instead of a clean error + exit 1.
merged_from: Because `plan_review_registry.by_id(repo_root)` is evaluated first and loads every active plan-review criterion prompt, asking to eval a code-review criterion can fail (crash or reject) due to an unrelated broken/malformed plan-review project criterion, even though the requested code-review criterion is well-formed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Import `CriteriaError` (e.g. `from rebar.llm.criteria.model import CriteriaError`) and broaden the handler to `except (LLMError, CriteriaError) as exc:`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Provide a way (e.g. a `--gate {plan_review,code_review}` flag) to disambiguate a criterion active in both gates, or document that the ambiguity is a hard, unrecoverable rejection.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:110-118: the `eval` subparser defines only `criterion_id`, `--runs`, `--output` — no gate selector
advisory.finding: A project criterion id that is legitimately defined in BOTH gates is permanently un-evaluable via `rebar criteria eval` — the ambiguity branch always returns 1 and there is no `--gate` flag to disambiguate.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an optional `--gate` argument that, when supplied, selects the gate and bypasses the ambiguity rejection.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the CLI's code-review activeness check with `calibrate_criterion`'s `repo_root is not None` guard so gate resolution is consistent when running outside a repo.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:152: `active_code_review = args.criterion_id in code_review_registry.effective_criteria(repo_root)` (evaluated even when repo_root is None)
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:417: `code_review_criterion = repo_root is not None and criterion_id in effective_criteria(repo_root)`
advisory.finding: The CLI's code-review activeness check uses `effective_criteria(repo_root)` while `calibrate_criterion` gates code-review resolution on `repo_root is not None and criterion_id in effective_criteria(repo_root)`; when `repo_root` falls open to None, the CLI may admit a packaged code-review id as active but `calibrate_criterion` will resolve it via the plan-review prompt mapping, producing a confusing missing-fixture error.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a malformed criteria overlay makes `rebar criteria eval` exit non-zero with a clean stderr message (no traceback).
evidence: tests added: `test_cli_admits_code_review_only_project_criterion`, `test_cli_rejects_unknown_criterion_with_distinct_message`, `test_cli_rejects_both_gates_as_ambiguous`, `test_cli_help_names_project_code_review_example` — ABSENCE: none exercises a malformed `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` that makes `effective_criteria`/`by_id` raise `CriteriaError`
advisory.finding: No test covers the malformed-overlay error path (a bad `activate`/`code_review` map), so the uncaught-`CriteriaError` regression is invisible to the suite.
